basic_identification.full_title: Refillable Welded Steel Cylinder for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) — Procedure for Checking Before, During and After Filling (द्रवित पेट्रोलियम गैस (एल.पी.जी.) के लिए पुनर्भरणीय वेल्डित इस्पात के सिलिंडर — भरणी प्रक्रिया: भरने से पहले, भरने के दौरान तथा भरने के बाद)
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Gas Cylinders (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee, MED 16, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard specifies the mandatory inspection, quality check, safety verification, and leak testing procedures to be adopted in LPG bottling plants and filling stations before, during, and after the filling of refillable welded steel LPG cylinders to ensure maximum transport and operational safety.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: None (New Standard developed to formalise the procedural safety checklists in LPG filling plants)

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Code of Practice / Requirements Standard (Mechanical Engineering Department / Gas Cylinders)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Certification and Procedural Compliance under the Gas Cylinder Rules of the Government of India, in coordination with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). All active LPG bottling plants must maintain strict audit logs verifying that 100% of filled cylinders pass the visual inspection, gross-weight verification, and soapy water leak checks mandated by IS 15966.

requirements.detail: Before filling, operators must visually check that the cylinder belongs to the authorized marketing company or distributor network to prevent illegal cross-filling.

Inspectors must verify that the cylinder's periodic hydrostatic test date (marked on the stay plate/collar) has not expired. Cylinders due or overdue for testing must be segregated immediately for periodic testing under IS 16054.
Mandates inspecting the cylinder shell for physical integrity prior to filling using strict rejection thresholds (bulges, cuts, dents, cracks, lamination, and digs).

A bulge is defined as a visible swelling of the cylinder wall, which alters the original calculated cylindrical geometry, representing a severe localized yielding under pressure. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.

A dent represents a localized depression. If the width of the dent is greater than 2 percent of the external cylinder diameter, the unit must be rejected if: a) its depth is greater than 1/10th of the mean dent diameter, b) its depth exceeds 25 percent of its width, or c) the dent lies on or adjacent to a weld joint.

A cut represents a sharp impression where metal has been removed or redistributed. It must be rejected if it is 75 mm or more in length, or if the undamaged remaining wall thickness is less than the minimum calculated wall thickness.
Intersecting cuts (the point of intersection of two or more cuts) represent a high-stress concentration zone susceptible to rapid crack propagation. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.

Cracks (splits or rifts in the shell) and laminations (layering of materials appearing as discontinuities) compromise the pressure-bearing capacity of low-carbon steel. Rejection is mandatory in all cases.
A dig represents a sharp depression where the surface metal has been physically penetrated. It must be rejected if its length is 75 mm or more and its width is 4 mm or more.
The actual weight of the clean, empty cylinder must be compared with the stamped tare weight. Abnormal tare weight variances indicate internal scaling or structural steel loss, requiring segregation.

Every cylinder must be checked for positive residual gas pressure. A completely depressurized cylinder indicates a potential open valve that may have allowed moisture, water, or air to enter, requiring internal washing and inspection.

Filled cylinders must be weighed to verify that the net LPG weight matches the rated filling capacity within narrow legal tolerances. Overfilled units represent an extreme thermal expansion hazard and must be safely degassed.

The valve, valve spindle, and bung-joint interface must be tested for leak tightness (using a soap-water solution or a dedicated testing bath). The presence of any bubbles indicating a leak requires immediate evacuation of the LPG.

Observed or calculated weights, test pressures, and dimension limits must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15966 : 2013 is the national Indian Standard prescribing procedural requirements and safety checking checklists to be adopted before, during, and after filling refillable welded steel LPG cylinders. Formulated under Sectional Committee MED 16, the standard serves as a critical safety buffer in LPG bottling plants. It mandates verifying cylinder ownership and periodic test due dates (re-testing at 2.45 MPa per IS 16054) before filling, and establishes strict visual rejection tables for cylinder wall defects (mandating rejection for any bulges, cracks, laminations, intersecting cuts, or deep dents). Post-filling, the standard enforces gross weight audits to prevent overfilling and requires a soap-water bubble test on all valves and bung joints to guarantee complete gas-tightness before the cylinder is sealed and dispatched to domestic or commercial kitchens.
